dialogue.content: こんにちは。相談役です。
dialogue.English: Hello. I'm your counselor.

dialogue.content: こんにちは。相談員です。
dialogue.English: Hello. I'm your counselor.

dialogue.content: こんにちは。
dialogue.English: Hello.

dialogue.content: どんなご相談ですか？
dialogue.English: What would you like to talk about today?

dialogue.content: 息子の事なんですけど…
dialogue.English: It's about my son...

dialogue.content: 息子さんのことですね。息子さんのどのようなことですか？
dialogue.English: I see, it's about your son. What about him is on your mind?

dialogue.content: 全然言う事聞かなくて。反抗期なのから？
dialogue.English: He doesn't listen to me at all. Is it because he's going through a rebellious phase?

dialogue.content: そうなんですね。息子さんはどのような時にいうことを聞かなくてお困りですか？
dialogue.English: I see. In what situations does your son not listen, and it's troubling you?

dialogue.content: 朝、私が大声で呼びないと起きて来ないし、同じ事言っても鼻でわらうだけでやろうとはしないですし、もう毎日イライラです！
dialogue.English: In the morning, he won't get up unless I call out loudly, and even if I repeat myself, he just scoffs and makes no effort to do it. It's so frustrating every single day!

dialogue.content: ご相談されている方は、お母さまでいらっしゃいますか？よろしければ、ご年齢を教えていただますか？
dialogue.English: May I confirm—are you his mother? If you're comfortable, could you tell me your age?

dialogue.content: 35歳です
ありがとうございます。毎日、大きな声で怒らないといけないのは、こちらもしんどいですね。息子さんはおいくつですか？
dialogue.English: Thank you. It must be exhausting for you to have to raise your voice every day. How old is your son?

dialogue.content: どうしたら言う事聞いて貰えるようになりますかね？  中1です
dialogue.English: How can I get him to listen to me? He's in the first year of junior high.

dialogue.content: 中学一年生なんですね。反抗期に入ったばかりですね。ご自宅ではお母さまだけにそのようなたいどなのでしょうか？
dialogue.English: The first year of junior high, I see. He's just entered his rebellious phase. At home, is his attitude like that only towards you?

dialogue.content: そうなんですよ～。主人は朝早くに会社に行って帰りも遅くて息子とは話す時間もないので、私に対してですね。
dialogue.English: That's right. My husband leaves for work early and comes home late, so he doesn't have time to talk with our son. So yes, it's directed at me.

dialogue.content: そうなんですね。
dialogue.English: I see.

dialogue.content: 話しかけても、話がうまくつながらないのは、お辛いですね。
dialogue.English: It must be hard when you try to talk to him, but the conversation doesn't really connect.

dialogue.content: そのうな反抗期が始まったのは、いつごろからですか？
dialogue.English: About when did that kind of rebellious behavior start?

dialogue.content: 私も息子が学校に行っている間はパートでいないんですけど、帰って来たら家も散らかってるし、片付けてないし
dialogue.English: I'm also out working part-time while he's at school, but when I get back, the house is a mess and he hasn't cleaned up...

dialogue.content: 中学生になった頃かしら
dialogue.English: Maybe around the time he started junior high.

dialogue.content: それは、お母さまもストレスですね。中学生になってからなんですね。
dialogue.English: That must be stressful for you. So, it started after he entered junior high.

dialogue.content: 疲れて帰って来てるのにそんな家みたりそんな態度されたらムカッいて大声で怒鳴りたくもなりますよ
dialogue.English: When I come home tired, see the house like that, and get that kind of attitude from him, it makes me angry enough to want to yell at the top of my lungs.

dialogue.content: そうですね。ご自宅ではそのようですが、学校での様子などはどのような感じかわかりすか
dialogue.English: I understand. That's how it is at home, but do you know what he's like at school?

dialogue.content: 小学生の頃は良く話してくれたけど、最近は学校の事を聞いても無視されちゃって…
dialogue.English: He used to talk to me a lot when he was in elementary school, but lately, when I ask about school, he just ignores me...

dialogue.content: そうなんですね。お仕事もあり、家に帰っても、イライラして毎日、大変ですね。
dialogue.English: I see. With your work and then coming home to this frustration, every day must be very difficult for you.

dialogue.content: そう思ってくれますか。それなのに誰も何も言って貰えないんですよ
dialogue.English: Do you really think so? It feels like no one acknowledges what I'm going through.

dialogue.content: 反抗期は親子の会話が少なくなりますが、一緒に過ごす時間がさらに少なくなるとお互いの距離も感じてしまいますよね。
dialogue.English: During the rebellious phase, parent-child communication tends to decrease, and if you spend even less time together, you can start to feel a distance between you.

dialogue.content: お母さまも、日頃のストレスを吐き出す場所がないのですね
dialogue.English: It sounds like you don't have an outlet for your daily stress either.

dialogue.content: そうなのかなぁ？
dialogue.English: I wonder if that's it.

dialogue.content: 休みの日は何だかんだ言って買い物付き合ってはくれますので、距離感はないでね
dialogue.English: On his days off, he'll still come shopping with me for one reason or another, so I don't think there's a distance between us.

dialogue.content: そうなんですね。優しい息子さんですね
dialogue.English: I see. He sounds like a kind son.

dialogue.content: 優しいところもあるんですよ。
dialogue.English: He does have his kind moments.

dialogue.content: 私の言い方も悪いからこう反抗してしまうのかしらね。
dialogue.English: I wonder if he's being so rebellious because there's something wrong with the way I talk to him.

dialogue.content: では、息子さんは、どんな時にイライラしていそうですか？
dialogue.English: So, in what situations does your son seem irritated?

dialogue.content: 私が怒ってガーって言っている時かしら
dialogue.English: I guess it's when I'm angry and nagging at him.

dialogue.content: そうなんですね。家では、なんでも話しやすくて態度に素直にでてしまうのかもしれませんね。
dialogue.English: I see. It might be that at home, he feels comfortable enough to express himself honestly through his attitude.

dialogue.content: 私がですか？
dialogue.English: Me?

dialogue.content: 息子かしら？
dialogue.English: Or my son?

dialogue.content: 失礼しました。息子さんです。
dialogue.English: My apologies. I meant your son.

dialogue.content: 今日はありがとうございました
dialogue.English: Thank you for today.

dialogue.content: こちらこそ、ありがとうございました。
dialogue.English: Thank you as well.
